160: ## 4. RULES
161: 
162: ### ✅ ALWAYS
163: 
164: 1. Verify Claude Code CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v claude`); check `$CLAUDECODE` for nesting.
165: 2. Use `--permission-mode plan` for review/analysis/exploration (no file writes); `--output-format text` unless JSON is specifically needed.
166: 3. Validate output before applying — correctness, completeness, alignment, syntax checks if code generated.
167: 4. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) to catch errors and warnings.
168: 5. Specify `--model` explicitly: default `claude-sonnet-5-5` unless task needs Opus (deep reasoning). Use Haiku only when explicitly requested or after adoption.
169: 6. Route to the appropriate `--agent <name>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table).
170: 7. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 interactively.
171: 8. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
172:    1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
173:    2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under "Tier 2 — Deep path"; do not re-enumerate it here.
174: 
175:    Tag the framework in the Bash invocation comment and use the returned `ENHANCED_PROMPT`. Apply the CLEAR 5-question check from the canonical card via the local delegating card.
176: 9. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — For code review or code generation, tell the dispatched session to:
177:    - Load `sk-code`.
178:    - Let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files.
179:    - Load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands.
180:    - Load `sk-code`'s code-review mode only for formal findings-first review output.
181:    - If the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set.
182:    - NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.
183: 10. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — For design or UI work, tell the dispatched session to:
184:    - Load `sk-design-md-generator`.
185:    - Extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md from the live source before building UI. Include named color tokens, type scale, components, and Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind.
186:    - Build against those measured tokens, then run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity.
187:    - If there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or exact tokens to build against.
188:    - NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority. The extraction measures real CSS; it does not judge design.
189: 11. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session.** When dispatching design or UI work:
190:    - Inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt. The child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference.
191:    - Include `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`.
192:    - If you cannot assemble the manifest — no Style Reference extracted or no live source to measure — ASK before launching the child. Do not start a silent design dispatch.
193:    - The child returns the demanded proof; the parent reconciles it on the return path.
194: 12. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).** By default, launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (`cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`).
195:    - Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return and verify outputs exist. Then SIGKILL the dispatcher process and any orphan children (`pkill -9 -f "claude -p"` for this skill, plus `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup).
196:    - Launch the next dispatch (this skill or a sibling) only after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
197:    - In a deep-flow session (deep-review / deep-research), the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start. Iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, not a per-iteration operator confirmation prompt.
198:    - Exception: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently and still SIGKILL each as its work returns.
199: 13. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env and state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable.
200:    - The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable. A child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question, writes nothing, and exits with code zero.
201:    - Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
202:    - A session may use the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `claude -p` run is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own.
203:    - The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set. Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 claude -p ...`. This is harmless when the wrapper is not in use.
204:    - See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
205:    - Prepend `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0` next to it so a dispatched child never inherits an enforced spec-gate from the parent shell. This is belt-and-suspenders alongside the wrapper's own neutralization and the core's complete `AI_SESSION_CHILD` classify/enforce no-op. Pattern: `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 claude -p ...`.
206: 14. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.
207:    - Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.claude/agents/<name>.md`, `.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime).
208:    - Map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default.
209:    - Claude Code has a native persona flag. Pass `claude -p --agent <name>`; the CLI resolves `.claude/agents/<name>.md` on the print path, which satisfies the rule.
210:    - On bare `claude -p` without `--agent`, INLINE the persona block into the payload using the in-payload pattern from `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 11). The child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
211:    - A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant. It silently drops the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract.
212:    - Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection". Native precedent: `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol".
213:    - Declare rare exceptions (native surface used, focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) at the dispatch site.
214: 
215: ### ⛔ NEVER
216: 
217: 1. Use `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` without explicit user approval (auto-approves all writes/tool calls).
218: 2. Trust output blindly for security-sensitive code (review for XSS, injection, hardcoded secrets, eval), or send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts — Claude Code transmits to Anthropic's API.

15: # Claude Code Agent Delegation Reference
16: 
17: Routing reference for delegating tasks from external AI assistants to specialized Claude Code CLI agents.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Core Principle
24: 
25: The calling AI decides WHAT to do, Claude Code decides HOW to do it within the delegated scope.
26: 
27: ### Purpose
28: 
29: Documents the active Claude Code agents in `.skilled/agents/` and how external AI assistants orchestrate them. The calling AI (OpenCode, Copilot, etc.) acts as the **conductor** (planner, validator, integrator) while Claude Code executes targeted tasks through its agent system.
30: 
31: ### When to Use
32: 
33: - Delegating supplementary implementation or analysis tasks to Claude Code agents
34: - Cross-AI code review or architectural second opinion via `@review`
35: - Deep reasoning and extended thinking via `@ai-council`
36: - Fresh-perspective debugging after the calling AI's attempts fail via Task-tool dispatch to `@debug`
37: - Codebase exploration in read-only mode via `@context`
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
42: 
43: ```
44: External AI (CONDUCTOR)               [OpenCode / Copilot / etc.]
45:   |
46:   |-- Analyzes task, selects Claude Code agent
47:   |-- Constructs claude CLI command with --agent flag
48:   |-- Delegates via Bash/shell execution
49:   |
50:   v
51: Claude Code CLI (EXECUTOR)
52:   |
53:   |-- Loads agent definition from .skilled/agents/<name>.md
54:   |-- Loads CLAUDE.md context hierarchy (global → project → local)
55:   |-- Executes with agent-specific instructions and tool permissions
56:   |-- Returns output to stdout
57:   |
58:   v
59: External AI (CONDUCTOR)
60:   |
61:   |-- Validates output quality and relevance
62:   |-- Integrates findings into its own workflow
63:   |-- Decides next step (accept, iterate, delegate elsewhere)
64: ```
65: 
66: ### Invocation Pattern
67: 
68: Claude Code agents are routed using the `--agent` flag with an agent name. Agent definitions live in `.skilled/agents/<name>.md` files. For read-only tasks, combine with `--permission-mode plan`.
69: 
70: ```bash

284: | Quick code review | `review` | sonnet (default) | `--permission-mode plan` |

291: ---
292: 
293: ## 6. BEST PRACTICES
294: 
295: ### Do
296: 
297: - **Match agent to task** — Use the routing guide above instead of generic prompts
298: - **Use `--permission-mode plan`** for all read-only agents (context, review, orchestrate, ai-council)
299: - **Include file references** with `@` for targeted analysis instead of broad prompts
300: - **Capture output** to files for multi-step workflows: `> /tmp/output.txt`
301: - **Use Opus for deep reasoning** but Sonnet for standard tasks to manage costs
302: - **Validate all output** before integrating into the calling AI's workflow
303: 
304: ### Don't
305: 
306: - **Don't delegate trivial tasks** — CLI overhead isn't worth it for simple questions
307: - **Don't skip validation** — Claude Code output needs review like any AI output
308: - **Don't use `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`** without explicit user approval
309: - **Don't nest Claude Code** — check `$CLAUDECODE` env var before invoking
310: - **Don't forget `2>&1`** — always capture stderr for error handling
311: - **Don't ignore costs** — use `--max-budget-usd` for batch operations

16: # Claude Code CLI Built-in Tools Reference
17: 
18: Reference for all Claude Code CLI capabilities, highlighting unique features and comparison with OpenCode.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: Delegate to Claude Code CLI for capabilities other AIs lack natively, especially extended thinking for deep reasoning, surgical diff-based code editing, schema-validated structured output, and cost-controlled execution with budget caps.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Covers all built-in capabilities of Claude Code CLI, highlights what is unique compared to other CLIs, and provides a comparison table for task routing decisions.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Choosing whether to delegate a task to Claude Code CLI vs handle it locally
35: - Understanding which Claude Code flags and modes to use for different task types
36: - Mapping calling AI capabilities to Claude Code equivalents
37: - Leveraging Claude Code-exclusive features (extended thinking, --json-schema, --permission-mode plan)
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. UNIQUE CAPABILITIES
42: 
43: ### Extended Thinking
44: 
45: **Deep extended-thinking reasoning.** Claude's extended thinking produces detailed internal reasoning before responding, leading to higher quality outputs for complex tasks. Do not assume the raw chain-of-thought is exposed verbatim in every output mode. Verify against the current `--output-format` and effort-level behavior before relying on internal reasoning being visible.
46: 
47: **Capabilities:**
48: - Multi-step logical reasoning with deeper internal deliberation at higher `--effort` levels
49: - Complex trade-off analysis across multiple dimensions
50: - Architecture design with consideration of constraints and alternatives
51: - Root cause analysis that traces through multiple code paths
52: - Mathematical and algorithmic problem solving
53: 
54: **Usage:**
55: 
56: ```bash
57: # Extended thinking with Opus (maximum depth)
58: claude -p "Design a real-time collaboration system for a document editor. Consider: CRDT vs OT, WebSocket vs SSE, conflict resolution, offline support, and scaling to 10K concurrent users." \
59:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --output-format text 2>&1
60: 
61: # Extended thinking with Sonnet (good balance)
62: claude -p "Analyze the trade-offs of our current caching strategy" \
63:   --effort high --output-format text 2>&1
64: ```
65: 
66: **Best For:**
67: - Architecture decisions that require weighing 4+ competing concerns
68: - Debugging subtle issues where surface-level analysis fails
69: - Algorithm design requiring correctness proofs or edge case analysis
70: - Technical decisions that will be hard to reverse
71: 
72: **Compared to other CLIs:** On OpenCode 1, reasoning capabilities come via provider-specific `--variant` reasoning effort (its own `--effort`-shaped lever). OpenCode 2 sets model and effort together with `-m provider/model#<level>`. Claude's `--effort` levels are especially strong for multi-dimensional trade-off analysis, but do not assume its internal reasoning is rendered as visible chain-of-thought without checking the current output mode.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ### Edit Tool (Built-in)
77: 
78: **Surgical diff-based code editing.** Claude Code's Edit tool makes precise, targeted changes to files: replacing specific strings without rewriting entire files.
79: 
80: **Capabilities:**
81: - Replace specific code blocks while preserving surrounding context
82: - Multi-file coordinated edits with dependency awareness
83: - Pattern-based replacements across files
84: - Preserves formatting, indentation, and file structure
85: 
86: **How it works:** When Claude Code generates a code change, it uses the Edit tool internally to apply surgical diffs rather than rewriting entire files. This means:
87: 
88: 1. Only changed lines are modified
89: 2. Surrounding context is preserved exactly
90: 3. Multiple edits to the same file are applied sequentially
91: 4. The calling AI receives the final result, not intermediate diffs
92: 
93: **Best For:**
94: - Precise refactoring (rename variable, extract function, change signature)
95: - Bug fixes that require changing specific lines without touching others
96: - Multi-file changes where files have interdependencies
97: 
98: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode has workspace-write sandbox but operates at file level. Claude Code's Edit tool is the most precise for surgical changes.
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ### Agent Tool (Built-in)
103: 
104: **Spawn focused subagents within a session.** Claude Code can internally create subagents for parallel or specialized tasks within a single session.
105: 
106: **Capabilities:**
107: - Spawn specialized subagents (explore, general-purpose, plan)
108: - Run parallel research tasks within a single session
109: - Isolate complex subtasks without context pollution
110: - Agent types: general-purpose, Explore (fast search), Plan (architecture)
111: 
112: **How it works:** When delegating a complex task to Claude Code, it may internally spawn subagents to handle subtasks. The calling AI doesn't need to manage this. It's transparent.
113: 
114: **Best For:**
115: - Complex tasks that naturally decompose into independent subtasks
116: - Research that requires exploring multiple code paths simultaneously
117: - Tasks where Claude Code needs to prototype before committing
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ### Structured Output (--json-schema)
122: 
123: **Schema-validated JSON output.** Claude Code can produce output that conforms to a JSON schema, guaranteeing structure for downstream processing.
124: 
125: **Capabilities:**
126: - Validates output against provided JSON schema before returning
127: - Supports complex nested schemas (objects, arrays, enums)
128: - Integrates with `--output-format json` for complete metadata
129: - Enables reliable pipeline integration
130: 
131: **Usage:**
132: 
133: ```bash
134: # Function analysis with guaranteed schema
135: claude -p "Analyze all exported functions in @src/utils.ts" \
136:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"functions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"params":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"returnType":{"type":"string"},"lineNumber":{"type":"number"},"complexity":{"type":"string","enum":["low","medium","high"]}},"required":["name","params","returnType"]}}}}' \
137:   --output-format json 2>&1
138: 
139: # Security audit with structured findings
140: claude -p "Audit @src/auth.ts for security issues" \
141:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"findings":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"severity":{"type":"string","enum":["critical","high","medium","low"]},"category":{"type":"string"},"line":{"type":"number"},"description":{"type":"string"},"recommendation":{"type":"string"}},"required":["severity","category","description"]}},"overallRisk":{"type":"string","enum":["critical","high","medium","low"]}}}' \
142:   --output-format json 2>&1
143: ```
144: 
145: **Best For:**
146: - Pipeline integration where downstream tools need guaranteed JSON structure
147: - Batch analysis producing machine-readable results
148: - Data extraction tasks that feed into automated workflows
149: - API response analysis with consistent output format
150: 
151: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode requests JSON via prompt instructions (no schema validation). Claude Code's `--json-schema` provides the strongest structural guarantee.
152: 
153: ---
154: 
155: ### Permission Mode: Plan (Read-Only)
156: 
157: **Safe read-only exploration mode.** `--permission-mode plan` restricts Claude Code to read-only operations: no file writes, no shell commands.
158: 
159: **Capabilities:**
160: - All read tools available (Read, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch)
161: - File writing and editing disabled
162: - Shell command execution disabled
163: - Safe for exploration, review, and analysis tasks
164: 
165: **Usage:**
166: 
167: ```bash
168: # Safe codebase exploration
169: claude -p "Analyze the architecture of this project" \
170:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
171: 
172: # Safe code review
173: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts for security issues" \
174:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
175: ```
176: 
177: **Best For:**
178: - Any task where the calling AI wants guaranteed read-only behavior
179: - Review and audit tasks where file modification would be inappropriate
180: - Exploration tasks before committing to implementation approach
181: 
182: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode has `--sandbox read-only` (similar concept).
183: 
184: ---
185: 
186: ### Cost Control (--max-budget-usd)
187: 
188: **Budget-capped execution.** Set a maximum dollar amount for a Claude Code session.
189: 
190: **Usage:**
191: 
192: ```bash
193: # Cap at $0.50
194: claude -p "Generate comprehensive tests for src/" --max-budget-usd 0.50 --output-format text 2>&1
195: 
196: # Cap at $2.00 for complex analysis
197: claude -p "Full security audit of the entire src/ directory" \
198:   --max-budget-usd 2.00 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
199: ```
200: 
201: **Best For:**
202: - Batch operations where costs could accumulate
203: - Experimentation without runaway spend
204: - CI/CD pipelines with cost budgets
205: 
206: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode has no built-in budget cap mechanism.
207: 
208: ---
209: 
210: ### Skills System
211: 
212: **On-demand specialized workflows.** Claude Code loads SKILL.md files that provide domain-specific instructions, reference materials, and routing logic.
213: 
214: **How it works:** Skills are loaded dynamically based on task intent. Each skill provides structured guidance including when to use, how to route, rules, and reference materials. This is an internal Claude Code capability. The calling AI doesn't invoke skills directly.
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ### Spec-Folder Continuity
219: 
220: **Persistent structured context across sessions.** Claude Code carries project context, decisions, and implementation history in the repository's spec folders rather than in a service.
221: 
222: **How it works:** `/speckit:save` writes continuity into the packet's canonical spec docs, `/speckit:search` retrieves it with the trigger index and the documented ripgrep recipes, and `/speckit:resume` walks `handover.md` -> `_memory.continuity` -> the spec docs. This enables Claude Code to recall prior decisions across sessions. The calling AI benefits because Claude Code can use historical project context that the calling AI doesn't have.
223: 
224: ---
225: 
226: ### Hooks
227: 
228: **Pre/post tool-call automation.** Configure shell commands that execute before or after specific tool invocations.
229: 
230: **How it works:** Hooks are configured in Claude Code's settings and fire automatically. For example, a hook could run linting after every file edit, or log every Bash command execution. This is transparent to the calling AI.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. COMPARISON TABLE
235: 
236: ### Claude Code vs OpenCode
237: 
238: Every OpenCode-side claim below is sourced from a live `opencode run --help` capture and `cli-opencode/references/cli-reference.md` (both current as of this fix). No claim is carried over unverified from an older comparison.
239: 
240: | Capability | Claude Code | OpenCode |
241: |------------|-------------|-----------|
242: | **Deep Reasoning** | `--effort` (low/medium/high/xhigh/max) | `--variant` (OpenCode 1 only): provider-specific reasoning effort, e.g. `high` default on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash`, up to `xhigh` on the `openai/gpt-5.6-*` family. OpenCode 2 sets model and effort together with `-m provider/model#<level>` |
243: | **Code Editing** | Built-in Edit tool (surgical diff-based) | Workspace-write sandbox via its own agent tool permissions |
244: | **Structured Output** | `--json-schema` (schema-validated) | `--format json` newline-delimited event stream (prompt-shaped, not schema-validated) |
245: | **Read-Only Mode** | `--permission-mode plan` (session-level flag) | No CLI-level read-only flag, achieved via a read-only agent's own tool permissions (e.g. the `context` subagent) |
246: | **Cost Control** | `--max-budget-usd` | No equivalent flag documented for `opencode run` |
247: | **Agent System** | 11 agents via `.claude/agents/*.md`, all directly invokable with `--agent <name>` | 11 agents via `.skilled/agents/*.md`, split into 3 classes: primary (`general`, `plan`, `orchestrate`, of which only `orchestrate` is a project file usable with top-level `--agent`), subagent (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`, routed via `--agent orchestrate`, never direct), and command-owned (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`, dispatched only by their parent `/deep:*` command) |
248: | **Session Continuity** | `--continue`/`-c`, `--resume [id]`/`-r`, `--fork-session` | `--continue`/`-c`, `--session <id>`/`-s`, `--fork` (all flags on `opencode run`, not standalone subcommands) |
249: | **File Attachment** | `--file <specs...>` (downloads named file resources at startup) | `-f`/`--file <files...>` (attaches files to the message) |
250: | **Memory System** | Spec-folder continuity docs via `/speckit:save` and `/speckit:search` | The same spec-folder continuity docs: `cli-opencode` dispatches load the project's full plugin/skill/MCP runtime, which is the skill's own primary value proposition. This is NOT an area where Claude Code has an advantage |
251: | **Hooks** | Pre/post tool-call hooks (configured in settings) | Not documented in the current cli-opencode skill surface, so it is unverified. Do not assume absence without checking `opencode`'s own docs |
252: | **Model Count** | 3 named tiers (opus, sonnet, haiku), each with dated release ids | Four providers, each with several models: `llmgateway` (default), `opencode-go`, `openai` and `minimax`. Per-model roster: [cli-opencode's providers reference](../../cli-opencode/references/providers-and-models.md) |
253: | **Auth Methods** | Claude subscription OAuth only: `claude auth login`, or `claude setup-token` (CI/CD). No API key | Per-provider `opencode providers login <provider>` / `opencode auth login` (OAuth-style) flows plus API keys |
254: | **Nesting Guard** | `$CLAUDECODE` env var + process ancestry + `~/.claude/state/<id>/lock` probe | `OPENCODE_*` env vars + process ancestry + a best-effort `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock` probe (ADR-001). OpenCode has its own three-layer guard, not "N/A" |
255: | **Non-Interactive** | `-p "prompt"` (print mode) | `opencode run "prompt"` (there is no separate `exec` subcommand) |
256: | **Background Exec** | `& 2>&1` (shell) plus the native `--bg`/`claude agents` background-session lifecycle | `& 2>&1` (shell) |
257: | **MCP Support** | Built-in, plus `--mcp-config` | `opencode mcp` subcommand for registrations, full runtime load on every `opencode run` dispatch |
258: 
259: ### When to Choose Each
260: 
261: | Need | Best Choice | Why |
262: |------|-------------|-----|
263: | Deep extended-effort reasoning | **Claude Code** | `--effort high`/`xhigh` with the most explicit reasoning-depth lever for this skill's default model |
264: | Surgical code edits | **Claude Code** | Edit tool operates at diff level |
265: | Schema-validated JSON | **Claude Code** | `--json-schema` guarantees structure. OpenCode's `--format json` is an event stream, not schema-validated |
266: | Read-only exploration | **Claude Code** | `--permission-mode plan` is an explicit CLI flag. OpenCode's read-only guarantee comes from agent-level permissions, not a CLI flag |
267: | Cost-controlled batch ops | **Claude Code** | `--max-budget-usd` built-in. No OpenCode equivalent documented |
268: | Full project runtime (plugins/skills/MCP/memory) in one dispatch | **OpenCode** | `cli-opencode`'s stated reason to exist: every `opencode run` loads the full project runtime |
269: | Multi-model / multi-provider flexibility | **OpenCode** | Many providers and models vs Claude Code's 3 named tiers |
270: | Native background-session lifecycle | **Claude Code** | `--bg` plus `claude agents` for managing background sessions, beyond plain shell `&` |
271: 
272: ---
273: 
274: ## 4. INTEGRATION TIPS FOR CALLING AIs
275: 
276: ### Combine CLI Strengths
277: 
278: External AIs can use multiple CLIs in a single workflow:
279: 
280: ```text
281: 1. OpenCode: Web research (--search flag)
282:    → Gather current information about a library or vulnerability
283: 
284: 2. Claude Code: Deep reasoning (extended thinking)
285:    → Analyze the research and design an implementation approach
286: 
287: 3. OpenCode: Code generation (sandbox-write)
288:    → Generate implementation based on Claude's plan
289: 
290: 4. Claude Code: Code review (--permission-mode plan)
291:    → Review the generated code for quality and security
292: 
293: 5. Calling AI: Final integration
294:    → Merge reviewed code into the project
295: ```
296: 
297: ### Output Parsing Patterns
298: 
299: ```bash
300: # Plain text — direct string
301: OUTPUT=$(claude -p "Review this code" --output-format text 2>&1)
302: 
303: # JSON with metadata
304: claude -p "Analyze functions" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.result'
305: 
306: # Schema-validated JSON

16: # Claude Code CLI Built-in Tools Reference
17: 
18: Reference for all Claude Code CLI capabilities, highlighting unique features and comparison with OpenCode.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: Delegate to Claude Code CLI for capabilities other AIs lack natively, especially extended thinking for deep reasoning, surgical diff-based code editing, schema-validated structured output, and cost-controlled execution with budget caps.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Covers all built-in capabilities of Claude Code CLI, highlights what is unique compared to other CLIs, and provides a comparison table for task routing decisions.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Choosing whether to delegate a task to Claude Code CLI vs handle it locally
35: - Understanding which Claude Code flags and modes to use for different task types
36: - Mapping calling AI capabilities to Claude Code equivalents
37: - Leveraging Claude Code-exclusive features (extended thinking, --json-schema, --permission-mode plan)
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. UNIQUE CAPABILITIES
42: 
43: ### Extended Thinking
44: 
45: **Deep extended-thinking reasoning.** Claude's extended thinking produces detailed internal reasoning before responding, leading to higher quality outputs for complex tasks. Do not assume the raw chain-of-thought is exposed verbatim in every output mode. Verify against the current `--output-format` and effort-level behavior before relying on internal reasoning being visible.
46: 
47: **Capabilities:**
48: - Multi-step logical reasoning with deeper internal deliberation at higher `--effort` levels
49: - Complex trade-off analysis across multiple dimensions
50: - Architecture design with consideration of constraints and alternatives
51: - Root cause analysis that traces through multiple code paths
52: - Mathematical and algorithmic problem solving
53: 
54: **Usage:**
55: 
56: ```bash
57: # Extended thinking with Opus (maximum depth)
58: claude -p "Design a real-time collaboration system for a document editor. Consider: CRDT vs OT, WebSocket vs SSE, conflict resolution, offline support, and scaling to 10K concurrent users." \
59:   --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --output-format text 2>&1
60: 
61: # Extended thinking with Sonnet (good balance)
62: claude -p "Analyze the trade-offs of our current caching strategy" \
63:   --effort high --output-format text 2>&1
64: ```
65: 
66: **Best For:**
67: - Architecture decisions that require weighing 4+ competing concerns
68: - Debugging subtle issues where surface-level analysis fails
69: - Algorithm design requiring correctness proofs or edge case analysis
70: - Technical decisions that will be hard to reverse
71: 
72: **Compared to other CLIs:** On OpenCode 1, reasoning capabilities come via provider-specific `--variant` reasoning effort (its own `--effort`-shaped lever). OpenCode 2 sets model and effort together with `-m provider/model#<level>`. Claude's `--effort` levels are especially strong for multi-dimensional trade-off analysis, but do not assume its internal reasoning is rendered as visible chain-of-thought without checking the current output mode.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ### Edit Tool (Built-in)
77: 
78: **Surgical diff-based code editing.** Claude Code's Edit tool makes precise, targeted changes to files: replacing specific strings without rewriting entire files.
79: 
80: **Capabilities:**
81: - Replace specific code blocks while preserving surrounding context
82: - Multi-file coordinated edits with dependency awareness
83: - Pattern-based replacements across files
84: - Preserves formatting, indentation, and file structure
85: 
86: **How it works:** When Claude Code generates a code change, it uses the Edit tool internally to apply surgical diffs rather than rewriting entire files. This means:
87: 
88: 1. Only changed lines are modified
89: 2. Surrounding context is preserved exactly
90: 3. Multiple edits to the same file are applied sequentially
91: 4. The calling AI receives the final result, not intermediate diffs
92: 
93: **Best For:**
94: - Precise refactoring (rename variable, extract function, change signature)
95: - Bug fixes that require changing specific lines without touching others
96: - Multi-file changes where files have interdependencies
97: 
98: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode has workspace-write sandbox but operates at file level. Claude Code's Edit tool is the most precise for surgical changes.
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ### Agent Tool (Built-in)
103: 
104: **Spawn focused subagents within a session.** Claude Code can internally create subagents for parallel or specialized tasks within a single session.
105: 
106: **Capabilities:**
107: - Spawn specialized subagents (explore, general-purpose, plan)
108: - Run parallel research tasks within a single session
109: - Isolate complex subtasks without context pollution
110: - Agent types: general-purpose, Explore (fast search), Plan (architecture)
111: 
112: **How it works:** When delegating a complex task to Claude Code, it may internally spawn subagents to handle subtasks. The calling AI doesn't need to manage this. It's transparent.
113: 
114: **Best For:**
115: - Complex tasks that naturally decompose into independent subtasks
116: - Research that requires exploring multiple code paths simultaneously
117: - Tasks where Claude Code needs to prototype before committing
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ### Structured Output (--json-schema)
122: 
123: **Schema-validated JSON output.** Claude Code can produce output that conforms to a JSON schema, guaranteeing structure for downstream processing.
124: 
125: **Capabilities:**
126: - Validates output against provided JSON schema before returning
127: - Supports complex nested schemas (objects, arrays, enums)
128: - Integrates with `--output-format json` for complete metadata
129: - Enables reliable pipeline integration
130: 
131: **Usage:**
132: 
133: ```bash
134: # Function analysis with guaranteed schema
135: claude -p "Analyze all exported functions in @src/utils.ts" \
136:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"functions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"params":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"returnType":{"type":"string"},"lineNumber":{"type":"number"},"complexity":{"type":"string","enum":["low","medium","high"]}},"required":["name","params","returnType"]}}}}' \
137:   --output-format json 2>&1
138: 
139: # Security audit with structured findings
140: claude -p "Audit @src/auth.ts for security issues" \
141:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"findings":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"severity":{"type":"string","enum":["critical","high","medium","low"]},"category":{"type":"string"},"line":{"type":"number"},"description":{"type":"string"},"recommendation":{"type":"string"}},"required":["severity","category","description"]}},"overallRisk":{"type":"string","enum":["critical","high","medium","low"]}}}' \
142:   --output-format json 2>&1
143: ```
144: 
145: **Best For:**
146: - Pipeline integration where downstream tools need guaranteed JSON structure
147: - Batch analysis producing machine-readable results
148: - Data extraction tasks that feed into automated workflows
149: - API response analysis with consistent output format
150: 
151: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode requests JSON via prompt instructions (no schema validation). Claude Code's `--json-schema` provides the strongest structural guarantee.
152: 
153: ---
154: 
155: ### Permission Mode: Plan (Read-Only)
156: 
157: **Safe read-only exploration mode.** `--permission-mode plan` restricts Claude Code to read-only operations: no file writes, no shell commands.
158: 
159: **Capabilities:**
160: - All read tools available (Read, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch)
161: - File writing and editing disabled
162: - Shell command execution disabled
163: - Safe for exploration, review, and analysis tasks
164: 
165: **Usage:**
166: 
167: ```bash
168: # Safe codebase exploration
169: claude -p "Analyze the architecture of this project" \
170:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
171: 
172: # Safe code review
173: claude -p "Review @src/auth.ts for security issues" \
174:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
175: ```
176: 
177: **Best For:**
178: - Any task where the calling AI wants guaranteed read-only behavior
179: - Review and audit tasks where file modification would be inappropriate
180: - Exploration tasks before committing to implementation approach
181: 
182: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode has `--sandbox read-only` (similar concept).
183: 
184: ---
185: 
186: ### Cost Control (--max-budget-usd)
187: 
188: **Budget-capped execution.** Set a maximum dollar amount for a Claude Code session.
189: 
190: **Usage:**
191: 
192: ```bash
193: # Cap at $0.50
194: claude -p "Generate comprehensive tests for src/" --max-budget-usd 0.50 --output-format text 2>&1
195: 
196: # Cap at $2.00 for complex analysis
197: claude -p "Full security audit of the entire src/ directory" \
198:   --max-budget-usd 2.00 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
199: ```
200: 
201: **Best For:**
202: - Batch operations where costs could accumulate
203: - Experimentation without runaway spend
204: - CI/CD pipelines with cost budgets
205: 
206: **Compared to other CLIs:** OpenCode has no built-in budget cap mechanism.
207: 
208: ---
209: 
210: ### Skills System
211: 
212: **On-demand specialized workflows.** Claude Code loads SKILL.md files that provide domain-specific instructions, reference materials, and routing logic.
213: 
214: **How it works:** Skills are loaded dynamically based on task intent. Each skill provides structured guidance including when to use, how to route, rules, and reference materials. This is an internal Claude Code capability. The calling AI doesn't invoke skills directly.
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ### Spec-Folder Continuity
219: 
220: **Persistent structured context across sessions.** Claude Code carries project context, decisions, and implementation history in the repository's spec folders rather than in a service.
221: 
222: **How it works:** `/speckit:save` writes continuity into the packet's canonical spec docs, `/speckit:search` retrieves it with the trigger index and the documented ripgrep recipes, and `/speckit:resume` walks `handover.md` -> `_memory.continuity` -> the spec docs. This enables Claude Code to recall prior decisions across sessions. The calling AI benefits because Claude Code can use historical project context that the calling AI doesn't have.
223: 
224: ---
225: 
226: ### Hooks
227: 
228: **Pre/post tool-call automation.** Configure shell commands that execute before or after specific tool invocations.
229: 
230: **How it works:** Hooks are configured in Claude Code's settings and fire automatically. For example, a hook could run linting after every file edit, or log every Bash command execution. This is transparent to the calling AI.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. COMPARISON TABLE
235: 
236: ### Claude Code vs OpenCode
237: 
238: Every OpenCode-side claim below is sourced from a live `opencode run --help` capture and `cli-opencode/references/cli-reference.md` (both current as of this fix). No claim is carried over unverified from an older comparison.
239: 
240: | Capability | Claude Code | OpenCode |
241: |------------|-------------|-----------|
242: | **Deep Reasoning** | `--effort` (low/medium/high/xhigh/max) | `--variant` (OpenCode 1 only): provider-specific reasoning effort, e.g. `high` default on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash`, up to `xhigh` on the `openai/gpt-5.6-*` family. OpenCode 2 sets model and effort together with `-m provider/model#<level>` |
243: | **Code Editing** | Built-in Edit tool (surgical diff-based) | Workspace-write sandbox via its own agent tool permissions |
244: | **Structured Output** | `--json-schema` (schema-validated) | `--format json` newline-delimited event stream (prompt-shaped, not schema-validated) |
245: | **Read-Only Mode** | `--permission-mode plan` (session-level flag) | No CLI-level read-only flag, achieved via a read-only agent's own tool permissions (e.g. the `context` subagent) |
246: | **Cost Control** | `--max-budget-usd` | No equivalent flag documented for `opencode run` |
247: | **Agent System** | 11 agents via `.claude/agents/*.md`, all directly invokable with `--agent <name>` | 11 agents via `.skilled/agents/*.md`, split into 3 classes: primary (`general`, `plan`, `orchestrate`, of which only `orchestrate` is a project file usable with top-level `--agent`), subagent (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`, routed via `--agent orchestrate`, never direct), and command-owned (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`, dispatched only by their parent `/deep:*` command) |
248: | **Session Continuity** | `--continue`/`-c`, `--resume [id]`/`-r`, `--fork-session` | `--continue`/`-c`, `--session <id>`/`-s`, `--fork` (all flags on `opencode run`, not standalone subcommands) |
249: | **File Attachment** | `--file <specs...>` (downloads named file resources at startup) | `-f`/`--file <files...>` (attaches files to the message) |
250: | **Memory System** | Spec-folder continuity docs via `/speckit:save` and `/speckit:search` | The same spec-folder continuity docs: `cli-opencode` dispatches load the project's full plugin/skill/MCP runtime, which is the skill's own primary value proposition. This is NOT an area where Claude Code has an advantage |
251: | **Hooks** | Pre/post tool-call hooks (configured in settings) | Not documented in the current cli-opencode skill surface, so it is unverified. Do not assume absence without checking `opencode`'s own docs |
252: | **Model Count** | 3 named tiers (opus, sonnet, haiku), each with dated release ids | Four providers, each with several models: `llmgateway` (default), `opencode-go`, `openai` and `minimax`. Per-model roster: [cli-opencode's providers reference](../../cli-opencode/references/providers-and-models.md) |
253: | **Auth Methods** | Claude subscription OAuth only: `claude auth login`, or `claude setup-token` (CI/CD). No API key | Per-provider `opencode providers login <provider>` / `opencode auth login` (OAuth-style) flows plus API keys |
254: | **Nesting Guard** | `$CLAUDECODE` env var + process ancestry + `~/.claude/state/<id>/lock` probe | `OPENCODE_*` env vars + process ancestry + a best-effort `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock` probe (ADR-001). OpenCode has its own three-layer guard, not "N/A" |
255: | **Non-Interactive** | `-p "prompt"` (print mode) | `opencode run "prompt"` (there is no separate `exec` subcommand) |
256: | **Background Exec** | `& 2>&1` (shell) plus the native `--bg`/`claude agents` background-session lifecycle | `& 2>&1` (shell) |
257: | **MCP Support** | Built-in, plus `--mcp-config` | `opencode mcp` subcommand for registrations, full runtime load on every `opencode run` dispatch |
258: 
259: ### When to Choose Each
260: 
261: | Need | Best Choice | Why |
262: |------|-------------|-----|
263: | Deep extended-effort reasoning | **Claude Code** | `--effort high`/`xhigh` with the most explicit reasoning-depth lever for this skill's default model |
264: | Surgical code edits | **Claude Code** | Edit tool operates at diff level |
265: | Schema-validated JSON | **Claude Code** | `--json-schema` guarantees structure. OpenCode's `--format json` is an event stream, not schema-validated |
266: | Read-only exploration | **Claude Code** | `--permission-mode plan` is an explicit CLI flag. OpenCode's read-only guarantee comes from agent-level permissions, not a CLI flag |
267: | Cost-controlled batch ops | **Claude Code** | `--max-budget-usd` built-in. No OpenCode equivalent documented |
268: | Full project runtime (plugins/skills/MCP/memory) in one dispatch | **OpenCode** | `cli-opencode`'s stated reason to exist: every `opencode run` loads the full project runtime |
269: | Multi-model / multi-provider flexibility | **OpenCode** | Many providers and models vs Claude Code's 3 named tiers |
270: | Native background-session lifecycle | **Claude Code** | `--bg` plus `claude agents` for managing background sessions, beyond plain shell `&` |
271: 
272: ---
273: 
274: ## 4. INTEGRATION TIPS FOR CALLING AIs
275: 
276: ### Combine CLI Strengths
277: 
278: External AIs can use multiple CLIs in a single workflow:
279: 
280: ```text
281: 1. OpenCode: Web research (--search flag)
282:    → Gather current information about a library or vulnerability
283: 
284: 2. Claude Code: Deep reasoning (extended thinking)
285:    → Analyze the research and design an implementation approach
286: 
287: 3. OpenCode: Code generation (sandbox-write)
288:    → Generate implementation based on Claude's plan
289: 
290: 4. Claude Code: Code review (--permission-mode plan)
291:    → Review the generated code for quality and security
292: 
293: 5. Calling AI: Final integration
294:    → Merge reviewed code into the project
295: ```
296:

298: 
299: ```bash
300: # Plain text — direct string
301: OUTPUT=$(claude -p "Review this code" --output-format text 2>&1)
302: 
303: # JSON with metadata
304: claude -p "Analyze functions" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.result'
305: 
306: # Schema-validated JSON
307: claude -p "List endpoints" --json-schema '{"type":"object",...}' --output-format json 2>&1 | jq '.result'
308: 
309: # Stream JSON for real-time
310: claude -p "Long analysis task" --output-format stream-json 2>&1 | while read -r line; do
311:     echo "$line" | jq -r '.type // empty'
312: done
313: ```
314: 
315: ### Error Handling
316: 
317: ```bash
318: # Robust invocation with error handling
319: OUTPUT=$(claude -p "$PROMPT" --output-format text 2>&1)
320: EXIT_CODE=$?
321: 
322: if [ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]; then
323:     echo "Claude Code failed (exit $EXIT_CODE): $OUTPUT"
324:     # Fallback strategy: try with simpler model or different approach
325: fi
326: 
327: # Check for nesting error
328: if echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "CLAUDECODE"; then
329:     echo "Nesting detected — cannot run Claude Code inside itself"
330: fi
331: ```

493: ## 13. MEMORY EPILOGUE
494: 
495: ### Purpose
496: 
497: Append this epilogue to any delegated prompt when the calling AI needs structured session memory back from Claude Code CLI. The agent will include the delimited section in its output, enabling the calling AI to extract, parse, and save it via `generate-context.js`.
498: 
499: ### Epilogue Template
500: 
501: Append the following text to the end of any Claude Code CLI prompt:
502: 
503: ```text
504: When you finish, include a session memory section in your output using EXACTLY this format:
505: 
506: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->
507: ## Session Memory
508: 
509: ### Summary
510: [1-3 sentences: what was accomplished]
511: 
512: ### Files Modified
513: - path/to/file.ts
514: 
515: ### Decisions
516: - Decision and rationale
517: 
518: ### Next Steps
519: - Remaining work
520: 
521: ### Spec Folder
522: [spec-folder-name, e.g. 015-outsourced-agent-handback]
523: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->
524: ```
525: 
526: ### Extraction by Calling AI
527: 
528: After receiving agent output, the calling AI extracts the handback section:
529: 
530: ```javascript
531: const match = output.match(/<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->/);
532: ```
533: 
534: Then constructs structured JSON and saves via:
535: 
536: ```bash
537: # Redact or scrub secrets before writing the JSON payload
538: # Write extracted data to JSON
539: cat > /tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json << 'JSONEOF'
540: {
541:   "specFolder": "<extracted or provided by calling AI>",
542:   "user_prompts": [
543:     "<delegated task or user goal>"
544:   ],
545:   "observations": [
546:     {
547:       "type": "implementation",
548:       "title": "<short accomplishment>",
549:       "narrative": "<what changed and why it matters>",
550:       "facts": [
551:         "<verification or durable implementation detail>"
552:       ]
553:     }
554:   ],
555:   "recent_context": [
556:     {
557:       "request": "<delegated task or user goal>",
558:       "learning": "<durable implementation detail or verification result>"
559:     }
560:   ],
561:   "recentContext": [
562:     {
563:       "request": "<compatibility alias for callers still emitting camelCase>",
564:       "learning": "<same semantics as recent_context>"
565:     }
566:   ],
567:   "FILES": [
568:     {
569:       "FILE_PATH": "<extracted path when known>",
570:       "DESCRIPTION": "<what changed and why it matters>",
571:       "ACTION": "Modified",
572:       "MODIFICATION_MAGNITUDE": "small",
573:       "_provenance": "tool"
574:     }
575:   ],
576:   "sessionSummary": "<extracted summary>",
577:   "keyDecisions": ["<extracted decisions>"],
578:   "nextSteps": ["<extracted remaining work>"],
579:   "triggerPhrases": ["<auto-derived from task>"],
580:   "toolCalls": [
581:     {
582:       "tool": "Read",
583:       "inputSummary": "<what was inspected>",
584:       "outputSummary": "<important result>",
585:       "status": "success"
586:     }
587:   ],
588:   "exchanges": [
589:     {
590:       "userInput": "<delegated request>",
591:       "assistantResponse": "<high-signal response excerpt>",
592:       "timestamp": "<ISO-8601>"
593:     }
594:   ]
595: }
596: JSONEOF
597: 
598: # Save via generate-context.js JSON mode
599: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json [spec-folder]
600: ```
601: 
602: Structured JSON is the required save path. You can pass the payload via temp file, `--stdin`, or `--json`. Do not call `generate-context.js` with only a spec folder. If `[spec-folder]` is passed on the CLI, that explicit target overrides any payload `specFolder`.
603: 
604: Accepted field names still include documented compatibility aliases such as `sessionSummary` / `session_summary`, `nextSteps` / `next_steps`, `userPrompts` / `user_prompts`, and `recentContext` / `recent_context`. Use the canonical field names shown above for new payloads. Persistence behavior for next-step fields: the first item becomes `Next: ...` and sets `NEXT_ACTION`, and additional items become `Follow-up: ...`.
605: 
606: If `/tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json` is passed explicitly and cannot be loaded, `generate-context.js` fails with `EXPLICIT_DATA_FILE_LOAD_FAILED: ...`. Do not fall back to OpenCode capture for that error.
607: 
608: Valid JSON can still be rejected after normalization. File-backed handbacks skip stateless alignment and `QUALITY_GATE_ABORT`, but thin payloads fail with `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` and cross-spec payloads fail with `CONTAMINATION_GATE_ABORT`.
609: 
610: Minimum viable payload: include a specific `sessionSummary`, at least one meaningful `recent_context` entry or equivalent observation, and `FILES` entries with a descriptive `DESCRIPTION`. Add `ACTION`, `MODIFICATION_MAGNITUDE`, and `_provenance` when known.

15: # Prompt Templates - Claude Code CLI

19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: This asset provides structured, copy-paste ready prompt templates for invoking Claude Code CLI across common development tasks. Each template includes the full command with flags, placeholder variables, and a concrete example.
24: 
25: ### Usage
26: 
27: 1. Find the template category matching your task
28: 2. Copy the command
29: 3. Replace `[placeholders]` with actual values
30: 4. Run in your terminal or via Bash tool

32: ### Flag Reference
33: 
34: | Flag | Purpose |
35: |------|---------|
36: | `-p "prompt"` | Non-interactive mode (required for cross-AI delegation) |
37: | `--output-format text` | Plain text output (default, recommended) |
38: | `--output-format json` | JSON output with metadata |
39: | `--model claude-sonnet-5-5` | Model selection (sonnet = default) |
40: | `--model claude-opus-5-5` | Deep reasoning model |
41: | `--model claude-haiku-5-5` | Fast/cheap model |
42: | `--permission-mode plan` | Read-only safe mode |
43: | `--json-schema '{...}'` | Schema-validated JSON output |
44: | `--max-budget-usd N` | Cost cap |
45: | `--agent NAME` | Agent routing |
46: | `--effort <level>` | Thinking effort: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max` |

493: ## 13. MEMORY EPILOGUE
494: 
495: ### Purpose
496: 
497: Append this epilogue to any delegated prompt when the calling AI needs structured session memory back from Claude Code CLI. The agent will include the delimited section in its output, enabling the calling AI to extract, parse, and save it via `generate-context.js`.
498: 
499: ### Epilogue Template
500: 
501: Append the following text to the end of any Claude Code CLI prompt:
502: 
503: ```text
504: When you finish, include a session memory section in your output using EXACTLY this format:
505: 
506: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->
507: ## Session Memory
508: 
509: ### Summary
510: [1-3 sentences: what was accomplished]
511: 
512: ### Files Modified
513: - path/to/file.ts
514: 
515: ### Decisions
516: - Decision and rationale
517: 
518: ### Next Steps
519: - Remaining work
520: 
521: ### Spec Folder
522: [spec-folder-name, e.g. 015-outsourced-agent-handback]
523: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->
524: ```
525: 
526: ### Extraction by Calling AI
527: 
528: After receiving agent output, the calling AI extracts the handback section:
529: 
530: ```javascript
531: const match = output.match(/<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->/);
532: ```
533: 
534: Then constructs structured JSON and saves via:
535: 
536: ```bash
537: # Redact or scrub secrets before writing the JSON payload
538: # Write extracted data to JSON
539: cat > /tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json << 'JSONEOF'
540: {
541:   "specFolder": "<extracted or provided by calling AI>",
542:   "user_prompts": [
543:     "<delegated task or user goal>"
544:   ],
545:   "observations": [
546:     {
547:       "type": "implementation",
548:       "title": "<short accomplishment>",
549:       "narrative": "<what changed and why it matters>",
550:       "facts": [
551:         "<verification or durable implementation detail>"
552:       ]
553:     }
554:   ],
555:   "recent_context": [
556:     {
557:       "request": "<delegated task or user goal>",
558:       "learning": "<durable implementation detail or verification result>"
559:     }
560:   ],
561:   "recentContext": [
562:     {
563:       "request": "<compatibility alias for callers still emitting camelCase>",
564:       "learning": "<same semantics as recent_context>"
565:     }
566:   ],
567:   "FILES": [
568:     {
569:       "FILE_PATH": "<extracted path when known>",
570:       "DESCRIPTION": "<what changed and why it matters>",
571:       "ACTION": "Modified",
572:       "MODIFICATION_MAGNITUDE": "small",
573:       "_provenance": "tool"
574:     }
575:   ],
576:   "sessionSummary": "<extracted summary>",
577:   "keyDecisions": ["<extracted decisions>"],
578:   "nextSteps": ["<extracted remaining work>"],
579:   "triggerPhrases": ["<auto-derived from task>"],
580:   "toolCalls": [
581:     {
582:       "tool": "Read",
583:       "inputSummary": "<what was inspected>",
584:       "outputSummary": "<important result>",
585:       "status": "success"
586:     }
587:   ],
588:   "exchanges": [
589:     {
590:       "userInput": "<delegated request>",
591:       "assistantResponse": "<high-signal response excerpt>",
592:       "timestamp": "<ISO-8601>"
593:     }
594:   ]
595: }
596: JSONEOF
597: 
598: # Save via generate-context.js JSON mode
599: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json [spec-folder]
600: ```
601: 
602: Structured JSON is the required save path. You can pass the payload via temp file, `--stdin`, or `--json`. Do not call `generate-context.js` with only a spec folder. If `[spec-folder]` is passed on the CLI, that explicit target overrides any payload `specFolder`.
603: 
604: Accepted field names still include documented compatibility aliases such as `sessionSummary` / `session_summary`, `nextSteps` / `next_steps`, `userPrompts` / `user_prompts`, and `recentContext` / `recent_context`. Use the canonical field names shown above for new payloads. Persistence behavior for next-step fields: the first item becomes `Next: ...` and sets `NEXT_ACTION`, and additional items become `Follow-up: ...`.
605: 
606: If `/tmp/save-context-data-<session-id>.json` is passed explicitly and cannot be loaded, `generate-context.js` fails with `EXPLICIT_DATA_FILE_LOAD_FAILED: ...`. Do not fall back to OpenCode capture for that error.

162: | **Stream JSON** | `--output-format stream-json` | Newline-delimited JSON for real-time processing |

164: ### Permission Mode Flags
165: 
166: | Mode | Flag | Behavior |
167: |------|------|----------|
168: | **Default** | (no flag) | Prompts for approval on writes and commands |
169: | **Accept Edits** | `--permission-mode acceptEdits` | Auto-approves file edits, prompts for shell commands |
170: | **Plan** | `--permission-mode plan` | Read-only — no file writes, no shell commands |
171: | **Don't Ask** | `--permission-mode dontAsk` | Skips unapproved tools silently |
172: | **Bypass** | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` | Auto-approves everything — **dangerous** |

174: ### Effort Level
175: 
176: | Level | Flag | Behavior |
177: |-------|------|----------|
178: | **Default** | (no flag) | The effort the child's settings give it, else the model's built-in default |
179: | **Low** | `--effort low` | Fastest, least detailed: classification, formatting, mechanical edits |
180: | **Medium** | `--effort medium` | Routine edits and short reviews |
181: | **High** | `--effort high` | Extended thinking for standard code generation, reviews and debugging |
182: | **Extra high** | `--effort xhigh` | Architecture, hard trade-offs, subtle root causes |
183: | **Max** | `--effort max` | The hardest problems, where cost is secondary; pair with `--max-budget-usd` |
184: 
185: Every model in the roster below takes all five levels. When to use each one → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md) §4.

187: ### Other Flags

192: | `--max-turns N` | Limit conversation turns |
193: | `--system-prompt "..."` | Override system prompt |

201: ## 6. MODELS
202: 
203: **Full model catalog with tiers, defaults, and `--effort` mapping → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**

205: ### Available Models
206: 
207: | Model | ID | Strengths | Cost | Best For |
208: |-------|----|-----------|------|----------|
209: | **Sonnet 5.5** | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Balanced; the **skill default** | Medium | General tasks, code generation, reviews |
210: | **Opus 5.5** | `claude-opus-5-5` | Deepest Opus reasoning; the deep-reasoning override, paired with `--effort high` | High | Architecture decisions, complex trade-offs, extended thinking |
211: | **Haiku 5.5** | `claude-haiku-5-5` | Fastest, most cost-effective | Lowest | Classification, formatting, simple queries, batch ops |
212: | **Fable 5.1** | `claude-fable-5-1` | The current Fable; the CLI's `best` alias | UNKNOWN | Work routed to the Fable family by name |

218: ## 7. SUBCOMMANDS
219: 
220: | Subcommand | Purpose | Example |
221: |------------|---------|---------|
222: | `claude agents` | List available agents | `claude agents list` |
223: | `claude auth` | Authentication management | `claude auth login` / `claude auth logout` |
224: | `claude mcp` | MCP server management | `claude mcp list` / `claude mcp serve` |
225: | `claude plugin` | Plugin management | `claude plugin list` |

231: ## 8. CONTEXT HIERARCHY (CLAUDE.md)
232: 
233: Claude Code automatically loads context from CLAUDE.md files in a hierarchy:
234: 
235: | Level | Path | Scope |
236: |-------|------|-------|
237: | **Global** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | All projects for this user |
238: | **Project** | `PROJECT_ROOT/CLAUDE.md` | Current project |
239: | **Local** | `SUBDIR/CLAUDE.md` | Current directory (additive) |
240: 
241: **Context loading**: All three levels are merged. Project and local instructions override global where they conflict. Local instructions are additive.
242: 
243: **File references**: Use `@./path/to/file` in prompts to include file contents:
244: 
245: ```bash
246: claude -p "Review @./src/auth.ts and @./src/middleware.ts for security issues" \
247:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1

250: ---
251: 
252: ## 9. STRUCTURED OUTPUT
253: 
254: ### JSON Schema Validation
255: 
256: Claude Code can produce schema-validated JSON output using `--json-schema`:
257: 
258: ```bash
259: claude -p "Analyze src/utils.ts" \
260:   --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"functions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"params":{"type":"string"},"returnType":{"type":"string"},"complexity":{"type":"string"}}}},"issues":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"line":{"type":"number"},"severity":{"type":"string"},"description":{"type":"string"}}}}}}' \
261:   --output-format json 2>&1
262: ```
263: 
264: ### Output Format Comparison
265: 
266: | Format | Use When | Parsing |
267: |--------|----------|---------|
268: | `text` | Human consumption, simple integration | Direct string |
269: | `json` | Programmatic processing with metadata | `jq` or JSON parser |
270: | `json` + `--json-schema` | Guaranteed structure for pipelines | Schema-validated parse |
271: | `stream-json` | Real-time processing, progress tracking | Line-by-line JSON |
272: 
273: ### Parsing JSON Output
274: 
275: ```bash
276: # Extract content from JSON output
277: claude -p "List functions in src/utils.ts" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.result'

279: # With schema validation
280: claude -p "..." --json-schema '{"type":"object",...}' --output-format json 2>&1 | jq '.result'
281: ```

286: 
287: ### Continue Last Session
288: 
289: ```bash
290: # Continue the most recent conversation
291: claude -p "Now apply the suggested fixes" --continue --output-format text 2>&1
292: ```
293: 
294: ### Resume Specific Session
295: 
296: ```bash
297: # Resume by session ID
298: claude -p "Continue where we left off" --resume SESSION_ID --output-format text 2>&1
299: ```
300: 
301: ### Fork Session
302: 
303: ```bash
304: # Fork from an existing session to try a different approach
305: claude --fork-session SESSION_ID -p "Try a different approach" --output-format text 2>&1
306: ```

308: ### Session IDs
309: 
310: Session IDs appear in JSON output format:
311: 
312: ```bash

314: claude -p "Start analyzing the auth module" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.session_id'
315: ```

318: 
319: ## 11. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
320: 
321: | Variable | Purpose |
322: |----------|---------|
323: | `CLAUDECODE` | Set when running inside Claude Code (nesting detection) |
324: | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` | Disable telemetry |
325: | `CLAUDE_MODEL` | Default model override |
326: 
327: ### Nesting Detection
328: 
329: **CRITICAL**: The `CLAUDECODE` environment variable is automatically set when running inside a Claude Code session. External AIs must check this before invoking:
330: 
331: ```bash
332: # Check for nesting — abort if already inside Claude Code
333: if [ -n "$CLAUDECODE" ]; then
334:     echo "ERROR: Cannot invoke Claude Code from within a Claude Code session"
335:     exit 1
336: fi
337: ```
338: 
339: ---
340: 
341: ## 12. TROUBLESHOOTING
342: 
343: | Issue | Diagnosis | Solution |
344: |-------|-----------|----------|
345: | `claude: command not found` | Not installed | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
346: | `401 Unauthorized` / not authenticated | Claude subscription OAuth not configured | Run `claude auth login` (or `claude setup-token` for CI/CD) |
347: | `Already inside Claude Code` | Nesting detected | Exit current session or use different terminal |
348: | Rate limit (429) | Too many requests | Wait for retry-after header; reduce frequency |
349: | Budget exceeded | `--max-budget-usd` cap hit | Increase budget or simplify prompt |
350: | Permission denied | Wrong permission mode | Use `--permission-mode plan` for read-only |
351: | Schema validation failed | JSON schema mismatch | Verify schema matches expected output structure |
352: | Context too large | Prompt + files exceed limit | Use `@` to reference specific files, not directories |
353: | Agent not found | Invalid agent name | Run `claude agents list` to see available agents |
354: | Session not found | Invalid resume ID | Check session ID from previous JSON output |
355: | Timeout | Long-running task | Use `--max-turns` to limit or run in background |
356: 
357: ### Common Patterns
358: 
359: ```bash
360: # Verbose mode for debugging
361: claude -p "..." --verbose --output-format text 2>&1
362: 
363: # Restrict tools for safety
364: claude -p "..." --allowedTools "Read,Glob,Grep" --output-format text 2>&1
365: 
366: # Cost-controlled execution
367: claude -p "..." --max-budget-usd 0.25 --output-format text 2>&1
368: ```

389: # Permission modes

391: claude -p "prompt" --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format text 2>&1   # auto-approve edits
392: 
393: # Structured output

405: 
406: # Background execution

408: ```

289: ```bash
290: # Continue the most recent conversation
291: claude -p "Now apply the suggested fixes" --continue --output-format text 2>&1
292: ```
293: 
294: ### Resume Specific Session
295: 
296: ```bash
297: # Resume by session ID
298: claude -p "Continue where we left off" --resume SESSION_ID --output-format text 2>&1
299: ```
300: 
301: ### Fork Session
302: 
303: ```bash
304: # Fork from an existing session to try a different approach
305: claude --fork-session SESSION_ID -p "Try a different approach" --output-format text 2>&1
306: ```
307: 
308: ### Session IDs
309: 
310: Session IDs appear in JSON output format:
311: 
312: ```bash
313: # Get session ID from JSON output
314: claude -p "Start analyzing the auth module" --output-format json 2>&1 | jq -r '.session_id'
315: ```
316: 
317: ---
318: 
319: ## 11. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
320: 
321: | Variable | Purpose |
322: |----------|---------|
323: | `CLAUDECODE` | Set when running inside Claude Code (nesting detection) |
324: | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` | Disable telemetry |
325: | `CLAUDE_MODEL` | Default model override |
326: 
327: ### Nesting Detection
328: 
329: **CRITICAL**: The `CLAUDECODE` environment variable is automatically set when running inside a Claude Code session. External AIs must check this before invoking:
330: 
331: ```bash
332: # Check for nesting — abort if already inside Claude Code
333: if [ -n "$CLAUDECODE" ]; then
334:     echo "ERROR: Cannot invoke Claude Code from within a Claude Code session"
335:     exit 1
336: fi
337: ```
338: 
339: ---
340: 
341: ## 12. TROUBLESHOOTING
342: 
343: | Issue | Diagnosis | Solution |
344: |-------|-----------|----------|
345: | `claude: command not found` | Not installed | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
346: | `401 Unauthorized` / not authenticated | Claude subscription OAuth not configured | Run `claude auth login` (or `claude setup-token` for CI/CD) |
347: | `Already inside Claude Code` | Nesting detected | Exit current session or use different terminal |
348: | Rate limit (429) | Too many requests | Wait for retry-after header; reduce frequency |
349: | Budget exceeded | `--max-budget-usd` cap hit | Increase budget or simplify prompt |
350: | Permission denied | Wrong permission mode | Use `--permission-mode plan` for read-only |
351: | Schema validation failed | JSON schema mismatch | Verify schema matches expected output structure |
352: | Context too large | Prompt + files exceed limit | Use `@` to reference specific files, not directories |
353: | Agent not found | Invalid agent name | Run `claude agents list` to see available agents |
354: | Session not found | Invalid resume ID | Check session ID from previous JSON output |
355: | Timeout | Long-running task | Use `--max-turns` to limit or run in background |
356: 
357: ### Common Patterns
358: 
359: ```bash
360: # Verbose mode for debugging
361: claude -p "..." --verbose --output-format text 2>&1
362: 
363: # Restrict tools for safety
364: claude -p "..." --allowedTools "Read,Glob,Grep" --output-format text 2>&1
365: 
366: # Cost-controlled execution
367: claude -p "..." --max-budget-usd 0.25 --output-format text 2>&1
368: ```
369: 
370: ---
371: 
372: ## 13. QUICK REFERENCE CARD
373: 
374: ```bash
375: # === ESSENTIAL PATTERNS ===
376: 
377: # Non-interactive (primary for cross-AI)
378: claude -p "prompt" --output-format text 2>&1
379: 
380: # Model selection
381: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-opus-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
382: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
383: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-haiku-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
384: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-fable-5-1 --output-format text 2>&1
385: 
386: # Effort (every roster model takes all five levels)
387: claude -p "prompt" --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort xhigh --output-format text 2>&1
388: 
389: # Permission modes
390: claude -p "prompt" --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1          # read-only
391: claude -p "prompt" --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format text 2>&1   # auto-approve edits
392: 
393: # Structured output
394: claude -p "prompt" --json-schema '{"type":"object",...}' --output-format json 2>&1
395: 
396: # Agent delegation
397: claude -p "prompt" --agent review --output-format text 2>&1
398: 
399: # Session management
400: claude -p "prompt" --continue --output-format text 2>&1
401: claude -p "prompt" --resume SESSION_ID --output-format text 2>&1
402: 
403: # Cost control
404: claude -p "prompt" --max-budget-usd 1.00 --output-format text 2>&1
405: 
406: # Background execution
407: claude -p "prompt" --output-format text 2>&1 &
408: ```
